children.value: QSVT transforms singular values through a sequence of a block-encoded matrix’s access circuit and projector phases

. For Hermitian matrices this applies a parity-constrained polynomial to signed eigenvalues. It avoids a phase-estimation register, while retaining the costs of normalization, spectral gap, polynomial accuracy, input access and success/readout.

children.value: projector phases. Its degree must be chosen from a promised normalized spectral gap and error. The accepted norm determines repetition/amplification work; arbitrary input and coefficient loading need actual constructions. General non-Hermitian inversion, singular-vector projectors and higher-accuracy phase synthesis remain outside this example.
The default Z trial has 11 CX, 12 continuous rotations, three measurements and dependency depth 28. The
includes all access/unprepare calls, four projector phases, both flag Hadamards and every failed full attempt.

At .03 statistical error and separate .005 statistical/no-acceptance allowances, its unexecuted ideal proposal uses 13,315 accepted samples and 88 attempts per slot: 1,171,720 complete attempts. Fresh input preparation is assumed; a single unknown specimen cannot be copied for retries.
supplies seven conditional Pareto points under the main page’s illustrative parameters. The .005 physical-fault allowance spans all attempts; the
synthesis-model scalar is per attempt. It reports factories, distances, peak qubits and serial runtime. Lower source counts or width do not alone establish a physical improvement.
No certified synthesis or conditional-output guarantee is provided.

The QDK mean fit is a cost model. Clean initialization timing/faults, classical preprocessing/compilation/readout and concrete synthesis are excluded. The main page states the separate norm certificate postselection would require. QASM is scoped to measured trials; the compiled global phase is recorded and may be omitted by export. It is not a phase-preserving controlled inverse oracle.

Tests include X, Y and multi-qubit words, real/complex preparation, X/Y/Z basis changes, recursive rejection of hidden nonunitary preparation, lowering and deterministic phase reproduction. A generic-spectrum test detects that the cubic is not an inverse. Independent review checked 15 Hermitian Pauli sums against independent Kronecker matrices.
